an4.115:1.1: “Monks, there are these four courses of action.
an4.115:1.3: There is the course of action that is unpleasant to do
an4.115:1.4: and that, when done, leads to what is unprofitable.
an4.115:1.5: There is the course of action that is unpleasant to do
an4.115:1.6: but that, when done, leads to what is profitable.
an4.115:1.7: There is the course of action that is pleasant to do
an4.115:1.8: but that, when done, leads to what is unprofitable.
an4.115:1.9: There is the course of action that is pleasant to do
an4.115:1.10: and that, when done, leads to what is profitable.
an4.115:2.1: “Now as for the course of action that is unpleasant to do and that,
an4.115:2.2: when done, leads to what is unprofitable,
an4.115:2.3: one considers it as not worth doing for both reasons:
an4.115:2.4: because the course of action is unpleasant to do,
an4.115:2.5: one considers it as not worth doing;
an4.115:2.6: and because the course of action, when done, leads to what is unprofitable,
an4.115:2.7: one considers it as not worth doing.
an4.115:2.8: Thus one considers it as not worth doing for both reasons.
an4.115:3.1: “As for the course of action that is unpleasant to do but that,
an4.115:3.2: when done, leads to what is profitable,
an4.115:3.3: it is in light of this course of action that one may be known—in terms of manly stamina, manly persistence, manly effort—as a fool or a wise person.
an4.115:3.5: ‘Even though this course of action is unpleasant to do,
an4.115:3.6: still when it is done it leads to what is profitable.’
an4.115:3.8: and thus the non-doing of that course of action leads to what is unprofitable for him.
an4.115:3.10: ‘Even though this course of action is unpleasant to do,
an4.115:3.11: still when it is done it leads to what is profitable.’
an4.115:3.13: and thus the doing of that course of action leads to what is profitable for him.
an4.115:4.1: “As for the course of action that is pleasant to do but that,
an4.115:4.2: when done, leads to what is unprofitable,
an4.115:4.3: it is in light of this course of action that one may be known—in terms of manly stamina, manly persistence, manly effort—as a fool or a wise person.
an4.115:4.5: ‘Even though this course of action is pleasant to do,
an4.115:4.6: still when it is done it leads to what is unprofitable.’
an4.115:4.8: and thus the doing of that course of action leads to what is unprofitable for him.
an4.115:4.10: ‘Even though this course of action is pleasant to do,
an4.115:4.11: still when it is done it leads to what is unprofitable.’
an4.115:4.13: and thus the non-doing of that course of action leads to what is profitable for him.
an4.115:5.1: “As for the course of action that is pleasant to do and that, when done, leads to what is profitable,
an4.115:5.2: one considers it as worth doing for both reasons:
an4.115:5.3: because the course of action is pleasant to do, one considers it as worth doing;
an4.115:5.4: and because the course of action, when done, leads to what is profitable, one considers it as worth doing.
an4.115:5.5: Thus one considers it as worth doing for both reasons.
an4.115:5.6: “These are the four courses of action.”
